subject.title: fix(sms): ack rate-limited Twilio callbacks instead of dropping them [AI]

question: May the SMS webhook return HTTP 200 for a signature-validated callback that OpenClaw intentionally does not dispatch, or must 2xx remain an admission guarantee?
rationale: Both overload choices have user-visible delivery consequences, and repository evidence does not establish an approved contract allowing OpenClaw to report successful acceptance while discarding the message.

options.title: Keep admission semantics
options.body: Preserve HTTP 429 unless the callback is accepted for processing, retaining Twilio failure and fallback visibility.

options.title: Queue before acknowledging
options.body: Add a bounded durable admission queue and return HTTP 200 only after the callback is safely recorded for later dispatch.

options.title: Approve drop-on-overload
options.body: Explicitly document and accept that valid messages above the quota are permanently discarded while Twilio receives HTTP 200.

recommendation.title: Keep admission semantics
recommendation.body: Preserve HTTP 429 unless the callback is accepted for processing, retaining Twilio failure and fallback visibility.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the current callback-quota behavior and is the strongest history-backed routing candidate for its acceptance semantics.
